newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firmer.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly stronger on Thursday but high sulphur cracked fuel oil was around unchanged, traders said.

Gasoline firmed with traders seeing local demand picking up after three weeks of weak buying interest. Buying was seen active for small cargoes of 5-10,000 tonnes for both 95 unleaded and low octane material. Prices for 95 unleaded were assessed at a premium of $4.50 over premium unleaded quotes fob Genoa.
Naphtha was seen firm after an Italian high paraffinic cargo fetched fob quotes high +$8 a tonne earlier in the week and a Tunisian cargo chnaged hands at fob quotes +$12.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil continued to linger around $108 fob Med with good supplies of product off setting limited demand.
"The Med is easier than the north which is looking tight," said one trader. Dealers said prices could well dip with no support seen from a lacklustre, albeit tighter NWE.
Low sulphur cracked fuel was supported around $132 cif Med with the main buyer understood to be discreetly interested. No weakness was seen in the short-term.
Russian high sulphur straight run has dried up, but low sulphur product was available around one percent quotes +$3.

Gas oil gained $1.25 on firmer futures but physical trade was quiet, with heating oil premiums notionally unchanged to slightly easier at high cif +$1.50 basis Genoa. The low sulphur diesel market remains well supplied with little buying interest.

State Algerian oil company Sonatrach lowered its price for low sulphur gas oil for December, asking for a premium flat to the formula from the $2.50 premium it obtained in November. The formula is based on diesel prices in northern Europe and the Mediterranean.
